asOf: Historical observation dates stated per event
note: Original Orbis factual annotations checked 14 October 2026; event-card links and scene-indexed notes identify the evidence. Points locate selected places approximately, not military fronts, camp boundaries or casualty-density surfaces. Contemporary coastlines are reference geography; modern country borders are hidden unless a scene explicitly compares country status. No comprehensive monthly occupation map is claimed.

items.title: London
items.text: The sustained Blitz on London began on 7 September 1940. Bombing damaged homes and infrastructure and killed civilians. The point locates London, without implying that all attacks struck one site or covered the entire city uniformly.

items.title: Coventry
items.text: The Luftwaffe attacked Coventry on the night of 14 November 1940. The cathedral was destroyed; its ruins remain a witness to the raid. This point locates the city rather than an invented bomb-impact grid.

items.title: Dresden
items.text: British bombing on the night of 13–14 February 1945 devastated Dresden, followed by US attacks. Naming the attackers matters when mapping civilian destruction. This city point does not estimate a firestorm perimeter or select among disputed casualty totals.

items.title: Hiroshima
items.text: The United States dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945. The National Archives documents destruction and large-scale loss of life. This point locates the city; it does not model a blast-radius circle or assign a precise death total.

items.title: Nagasaki
items.text: The United States bombed Nagasaki on 9 August 1945. The two cities experienced different terrain and attack conditions. This chapter identifies the dates and cities without treating them as interchangeable casualty measurements.
